quotes.text: Treat a copilot response like work prepared by a junior colleague. It may save you time, but your name still goes on the email, the case update, or the approval.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable rule of thumb for owning AI-generated output.

quotes.text: A copilot helps you ask, understand, draft, and decide. An agent focuses on a defined piece of work that it can carry out on the rules set by the business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a crisp line between copilots and agents.

quotes.text: Co-pilot follows the access rules already attached to the signed-in user. If you cannot open a customer record, co-pilot should not pull details from that record into an answer for you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the permission model behind Copilot answers in plain terms.

quotes.text: Do not let an AI draft decide a refund, a payment, a contract promise, or a company policy. Those decisions need a person who understands the full situation and can be held accountable for the result.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation on where human accountability must remain.

chapters.title: Dynamics 365 as the foundation: CRM and ERP
What Copilot actually does: summarize, answer, draft
Sales: preparing for the next customer conversation
Customer service: from long case histories to next steps
Conclusion: the helper inside each business room

takeaways: Copilot in Dynamics 365 works inside the business records people already use, summarizing histories, answering questions about permitted data and preparing first drafts.
Each Dynamics 365 app (Sales, Customer Service, Finance and Operations, Business Central) has its own Copilot features and task-focused agents, distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Copilot follows the signed-in user's access rules, and people must review drafts and stay accountable for refunds, payments, promises and approvals.
hook: Sales calls, service cases, invoices and orders bury the facts people need under notes, emails and menus. This Simply Explained episode shows business users and decision makers how Copilot in Dynamics 365 summarizes records, answers questions and prepares drafts across Sales, Customer Service, Finance and Business Central, and why human approval stays essential.
